title: People, teams, and agent apps
blurb: Employees, proficiency, digital attributes, and the agent applications the help pages still name.

lessons.title: Employee profiles
lessons.summary: An employee has a first name, last name, an email-shaped username, and a primary role. Special characters the getting-started page lists are rejected in names.
objectives: Create an employee with the required fields

p: Admin, Employees, Create Employee. First and last name are required. Middle name is optional. The page says special characters are not accepted in those fields, including ! / < > ? % and the double quote.
The username must be in the form of an email address and is filled from the email field. You can edit it. Assign a primary role. Create saves the profile. Create & Invite sends the activation mail.
A person who will log in needs a login authenticator, selected on the Security tab when you are setting up OpenID Connect. A back-end application employee must not have one.
The Access Keys tab appears after the account exists. The Avaya page says to activate the account, then generate the key.

steps.label: Activation
steps.detail: The user sets a password from the mail.

steps.label: Authenticator
steps.detail: Without it, the page says the employee cannot log in.

steps.label: No key yet
steps.detail: Keys are a later, separate step for applications.

quiz.why: The page gives that list and says it is not exhaustive.

quiz.why: It is auto-filled from the email address and can be edited.

quiz.why: Create alone saves the profile for more editing.

quiz.q: Who must have a login authenticator?
quiz.why: The page says employees can only log in if they have one, and API accounts should not.

quiz.q: When does the Access Keys tab show up, on the Avaya page?
choices: After the account is created and activated
quiz.why: The page says the tab appears after account creation, and activation matters.

quiz.q: Middle name is…
quiz.why: First and last are required.

Sends the activation email.
Required for humans. Forbidden for back-end apps.
The page lists ! / < > ? % and the double quote in names.

steps: Human: real-looking synthetic name, email username, primary role, authenticator, Create & Invite.
Connector: name with no banned characters, role with two permissions, no authenticator.

lessons.title: Assign a skill and a proficiency
lessons.summary: Assignment is not complete at the skill name. Bullseye needs a proficiency from 1 to 20, and 1 is best. The Classics example starts at 1–5 and widens to 1–8.
objectives: Use the routing simulator to watch it

figure.caption: Classics, Inc. fiction skill, from the bullseye page

p: On the bullseye page, Marguerite sets the fiction skill's REQAGENT to HighProficiency 1 and LowProficiency 5. Music plays for 90 seconds. UpdateContact then sets HighProficiency 1 and LowProficiency 8. Agents scored 6, 7, or 8 become eligible only after the wait.
She assigned proficiency from fluency, and she checked it before editing the script. Proficiency can be set on the ACD user profile or the skill record.

UPDATE CONTACT DIGITAL says the highest proficiency an agent must have, and the lowest, are whole numbers from 1 to 20, 1 best and 20 worst. Digital priority on that action does not accelerate. The page says to use workflow automation if you need to change digital priority.
The simulator in this lab uses the same window. Its longest-idle tie-break is labeled as a classroom rule.

steps.label: Deliver
steps.detail: An agent at proficiency 7 can now match.

quiz.q: Classics opening window?
quiz.why: That is the fiction skill example.

quiz.q: What happens at 90 seconds in that example?
quiz.why: Music, then UpdateContact.

quiz.q: Proficiency 20 means…
quiz.why: Both the bullseye page and the digital update page say 1 is best and 20 is worst.

quiz.q: Where can you assign proficiency?
choices: ACD user profile or skill record
quiz.why: The bullseye key facts say either.

quiz.q: Digital Update Contact acceleration?
choices: The page says digital priority has no acceleration
quiz.why: Change digital priority with workflow automation if you need to.

quiz.q: An agent at proficiency 7 during the first 90 seconds of the Classics script is…
quiz.why: They join after the window widens to 8.

cards.back: The scale. Do not invert it.
The best end of the window. Usually the smaller number.
The Music wait in the Classics example.
The action that widens the window.

lab.title: Run the Classics window
steps: Set high 1, low 5, widen-after 90, widened low 8.
Give one agent proficiency 2 and another 7.
Step until 90 seconds and confirm the proficiency 7 agent is out, then in.
Read the trace. Remember longest-idle is this lab's tie-break.
lab.done: The trace matches the help page's story.

faults.title: Window never widens
faults.symptom: Wait time passes 90 seconds and only proficiency 1–5 are offered.
faults.cause: The second action from the example was never added.
faults.fix: Add UpdateContact with low 8, or whatever window operations agreed, after the Music wait.

lessons.title: MAX and Agent Workspace
lessons.summary: Current help still names MAX and a family of Agent Workspace applications. Digital support is not identical across them. AutoSummary lists the ones it works with.
objectives: Include MAX when the page includes MAX

p: Agents use MAX or the Agent Workspace suite. The page says MAX supports all available digital channels. Support inside the Agent Workspace suite depends on the application, and you should read that application's details.
They also need channel permissions, the Digital Engagement attribute, and the skill or queue.
The AutoSummary overview says it works with Agent Workspace (Agent), the browser extension (Agent Integrated), embedded (Agent Embedded), Microsoft Teams, Salesforce Agent, and MAX.

Using it on MAX requires a Copilot for Agents license as well as AutoSummary enablement. The 26.2 rename table is a separate, moving list. Do not delete MAX from a design because a rename row exists for a different product.

lessons.title: Who can see a recording
lessons.summary: Seeing a recording is a permission question. The Admin page says agents may see only their own interactions while supervisors see more. Recording Management is a separate product surface.
objectives: Know hold audio is absent even for people who can play the file

p: The Admin page says access to recordings and interactions is typically permission-based. Agents may view only their own. Supervisors or administrators may see a team or more. You review those permissions for operations and for compliance.
A user who cannot find a recording may be outside their view, not looking at a failed recorder.
Recording Management says calls on hold are not recorded. The recording stops on hold, including hold music, and resumes when the agent returns. A consultation during hold is recorded.

Stereo is the default, and mono is supported. Stereo lets you use analytics, keep participants separate, and play one side. The page tells you to ask your account representative if you have questions.

flow.title: An agent cannot find a call

steps.label: Check the role
steps.detail: Own interactions only is a normal setting.

steps.label: Supervisor search
steps.detail: A broader role should see the team.

quiz.q: Agent visibility, in the Admin page's example?
choices: They may see only their own interactions
quiz.why: Supervisors may see more. It is a permission.

quiz.q: Hold audio in the recording?
choices: Not captured. Recording resumes when the agent returns.
quiz.why: Recording Management is explicit.

quiz.q: Default channel layout?
quiz.why: Stereo is the default. Ask the account representative if you need a decision.

quiz.q: A consultation while the caller is on hold…
quiz.why: The page distinguishes hold audio from consultation audio.

quiz.q: A missing recording in the agent app is first…
quiz.why: The Admin page makes visibility a permission.

quiz.q: Playing one side of a call depends on…
quiz.why: The page lists that as a reason to use stereo.

cards.back: A normal agent permission, not an outage.
Expected. Music on hold is not in the file.
Recorded even during the caller's hold.
Separate participants. Mono is available.

lab.title: Classify three gaps
steps: Agent cannot see a teammate's call. Mark permission.
A file has silence where hold music played. Mark expected.
A supervisor with team access finds no file and no hold. Mark investigate recording, not the agent role.
Write the stereo sentence under the file that must support analytics.
lab.done: The three gaps have three different owners.

lessons.title: Teams, views, and what we will not invent
lessons.summary: Supervisors are described as having broader visibility. The Admin page also names views as a security tool. This lesson does not invent a team-hierarchy feature the page does not describe.
objectives: Use the word view as the page does
Separate team visibility from a guessed org chart
Ask for the current view help before a design

p: The Admin page lists views next to roles, login authenticators, and access keys as the way you manage security and data access. It says agents may see their own interactions and supervisors may have broader visibility across teams or business units.
It does not, in that passage, define how a team record is created or how a view is filtered. Those steps need the current view and team help pages. This lab will not invent the click path.

A bullseye pool is about proficiency and attributes, not about the supervisor's team. A WFM schedule is about staffing. A view is about who can see data. Three different 'groups' get confused in design reviews.
When you say team, say which product's team you mean.

steps.label: Say which
steps.detail: The word team alone is ambiguous.

quiz.q: Views are listed beside what, on the Admin page?
choices: Roles, login authenticators, and access keys
quiz.why: That is the security toolset the page names.

quiz.q: Does this lesson include a click-path for creating a team?
choices: No. That path was not in the cited passage.
Yes. Teams are created under Studio.
quiz.why: Look up the current page rather than memorizing a path from this lab.

quiz.why: Do not implement bullseye by editing a view.

quiz.q: Broader supervisor visibility is described as…

Limited to their own calls only, always
quiz.why: The page says 'may', and it is a permission design.

quiz.q: IEX and CXone WFM…
quiz.why: The WFM welcome page separates them.

quiz.q: Saying 'team' in a design review without a product…
quiz.why: Name the product.

The agent example.
The supervisor example. Still a permission.

lessons.title: Make one agent digitally ready
lessons.summary: Four checks: supported app, channel permission, Digital Engagement, and the digital skill. Missing any one of them looks like a routing bug.

p: Digital Channels lists the agent requirements together: a supported application, permissions for each channel, the Digital Engagement attribute, and assignment to the routing queues or digital skills that handle the channel.
New inbound configuration should be the skill, not a new routing queue. The agent line still mentions queues because old queues remain and stay synced with skills.
After the four checks, send one inbound contact on that channel. If it queues on the default digital skill and the agent is available inside any bullseye window, the agent should be offerable.
If the script retargets to a second digital skill, the agent needs that skill too. The default skill on the POC is only the start.

steps.label: App
steps.detail: MAX, or a Workspace app you verified.

quiz.q: How many of the four checks are optional?
choices: None. The page lists them as requirements.
quiz.why: App, permission, attribute, and skill or queue.

quiz.q: New inbound digital work should add…
quiz.why: You cannot create new routing queues. Old ones remain.

quiz.q: The POC default skill is…
choices: The starting skill. The script may change it.
The only skill that will ever be used
quiz.why: Digital routing describes that pattern.

quiz.q: MAX, for digital, according to the page?
quiz.why: Workspace apps need their own check.

quiz.q: An agent on the default skill who misses the script's retarget skill…
choices: Will not be offered that contact
quiz.why: Delivery follows the skill the script requests.

quiz.q: Old routing queues…
choices: Were deleted in 2020 with no remainder
quiz.why: The page says the lists stay consistent.

cards.back: App, permission, Digital Engagement, skill.
Start, not necessarily the final skill.
For new inbound digital work.
Old queues and digital skills stay aligned.

lessons.title: ScreenAgent beside the voice recording
lessons.summary: ScreenAgent records the screen. From version 2.1.40 it can mask the screen when voice is masked, so a paused voice recording does not leave the sensitive screen in the file.

p: Recording Management supports audio and screen for quality and compliance. ScreenAgent records and monitors screen activity. The page points at separate install topics for Windows and for Mac, which this lesson does not copy.

During masking, screen recording can be masked for all participants when the voice interaction is masked, so sensitive data is not left on the digital recording. The page says this is available with ScreenAgent 2.1.40 and later.

sections.h: Not the same gap as hold
p: Hold stops voice recording. Masking hides content while recording policy says the content is sensitive. A reviewer should say which of the two they are looking at.
Third-party telephony recording is a further path, through Engagement Hub, and it has its own supported-deployment table. It is not ScreenAgent.

steps.label: Play
steps.detail: Sensitive digits should not remain on screen.

steps.label: Hold is different
steps.detail: Hold is a stop, not a mask.

quiz.q: ScreenAgent 2.1.40 adds what, in the page's words?
choices: Screen masking when the voice interaction is masked
quiz.why: So sensitive data is not transferred via the screen recording.

quiz.q: Install steps for ScreenAgent in this lesson are…
choices: Not copied. The page points at Windows and Mac topics.
quiz.why: Open those topics for the procedure.

quiz.q: Hold versus mask?
choices: Hold stops recording. Mask hides sensitive content.
quiz.why: Do not ticket one as the other.

quiz.q: Engagement Hub recording is…
choices: A path for third-party telephony, not ScreenAgent
quiz.why: The recording page points third-party telephony at Engagement Hub.

quiz.q: Stereo is…
quiz.why: The page says stereo by default, mono supported.

quiz.q: QM uses recordings for…
choices: Quality processes and compliance, as the page frames it
quiz.why: That is the opening sentence of Recording Management.

cards.back: Screen recording and monitoring. Install topics are separate.
Screen can mask when voice masks.
Recording stops. Not a mask.
Third-party telephony into CXone, including recording.
